body:
Was recently visiting this bug, its still the number one reason why we can't really default to DirectX on Windows.
It is probably the same as in #103501

I guess I have a solution albeit it may or may not be pretty:

Debugging further I realized that the bug is coming from the driver when creating too many of these (!CPU only)  DescriptorHeaps.

While the documentation doesn't say so, it seems that at least for the Nvidia driver there is some hard limit on how many of these can be created. I'm not sure if this limit is constant or frame based.
As it seems that most applications only use a few, its probably not well tested what happens if one creates a few thousands of them.

Pooling them didn't help as well, as we are still stuck with trying to allocate a lot of them in a single frame (I am not sure if this max count is constant over time)

While trying to find other implementations I stumbled across the SDL3 DirectX12 driver  [SDL3](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/fdc4f8fa390c872da17c21bdbe35ce4cf2da25d2/src/gpu/d3d12/SDL_gpu_d3d12.c#L2202).

They do separate GPUDescriptorHeaps and CPU-only DescriptorHeaps[StagingDescriptorHeap].  
While instead of always recreating the latter, creating them at a size of 1024 entries per heap and then distributing the individual D3D12_CPU_DESCRIPTOR_HANDLEs feeding them back to a free list. 


Implementing this via a fixed block size pool in the DirectX12 backend of Godot, seemed to fix the crash from our side.
I will try to make a PR out of this, but neither my C++ nor DirectX  are up par so it may be more of a starting point for others to pick up.
